---
title: "Price volatility"
subtitle: "How much prices move within the day and between markets"
execute:
  echo: false
  freeze: false
---

```{python}
#| label: setup
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import HTML, Markdown

ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "_quarto.yml").exists():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import chart_style as cs

d = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data/processed/core_daily.csv", parse_dates=["date"]).set_index("date")
m = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data/processed/core_monthly.csv", parse_dates=["month"]).set_index("month")
d = d[d["hours_with_price"] >= 20]
last = d.index.max()
S = cs.SURF[cs.MODE]
fmt = lambda v, dec=0: "–" if pd.isna(v) else f"{v:,.{dec}f}"

# Exchange rate implied by EPİAŞ's own TL and EUR prices, to show lira gaps in euros.
for df in (d, m):
    fx = df["ptf_mean"] / df["ptf_eur_mean"].where(df["ptf_eur_mean"] > 0)
    for col in ("smf_ptf_gap", "gap_when_short", "gap_when_long", "aof_ptf_gap", "smf_ptf_absgap"):
        df[col + "_eur"] = df[col] / fx
# Gaps as a share of the period's average PTF. Ratios of averages, not averages of hourly ratios:
# hourly percentages explode when PTF is near zero.
for df in (d, m):
    for col in ("smf_ptf_gap", "gap_when_short", "gap_when_long", "aof_ptf_gap"):
        df[col + "_pct"] = df[col] / df["ptf_mean"].where(df["ptf_mean"] > 0) * 100
m["ptf_spread_pct"] = m["ptf_spread"] / m["ptf_mean"] * 100
m["ptf_std_pct"] = m["ptf_std"] / m["ptf_mean"] * 100
full = m["hours_with_price"] >= m.index.days_in_month * 24 - 1
mf = m[full]
```

```{python}
#| label: tiles
w30 = d.loc[last - pd.Timedelta(days=29): last]
w30_ly = d.loc[last - pd.DateOffset(years=1) - pd.Timedelta(days=29): last - pd.DateOffset(years=1)]
y12 = d.loc[last - pd.DateOffset(years=1) + pd.Timedelta(days=1): last]
zero_ytd = d.loc[f"{last.year}-01-01":, "ptf_zero_hours"].sum()
zero_ly = d.loc[f"{last.year - 1}-01-01": last - pd.DateOffset(years=1), "ptf_zero_hours"].sum()
tiles = [
    ("Daily PTF spread, last 30 days", f"{w30['ptf_spread_eur'].median():.1f} EUR/MWh",
     f"median of daily max − min · {w30_ly['ptf_spread_eur'].median():.1f} a year earlier"),
    ("Balancing gap, last 12 months", f"+{y12['gap_when_short_eur'].mean():.1f} / −{abs(y12['gap_when_long_eur'].mean()):.1f} EUR/MWh",
     "SMF − PTF when the system was short / long"),
    (f"Zero-price hours in {last.year}", f"{zero_ytd:,.0f} hours",
     f"{zero_ly:,.0f} in the same period of {last.year - 1}"),
]
HTML('<div class="tile-grid">' + "".join(
    f'<div class="tile"><p class="eyebrow">{a}</p><h3>{b}</h3><p>{c}</p></div>' for a, b, c in tiles) + "</div>")
```

## Daily price spread

The daily spread is the gap between the most and the least expensive hour of the day-ahead price. It is a first estimate of what a battery could earn from buying in the cheapest hour and selling in the most expensive one, before efficiency losses, fees and the limits of the battery. The second line, the standard deviation, measures how far hourly prices move around the day's average. Both are monthly averages of daily values. Euros (the default) make years comparable; lira values rise with inflation. The percentage view divides by the month's average PTF, so it shows spread relative to the price level: a spread of 100% means the gap between the cheapest and the dearest hour equals the average price.

```{python}
#| label: spread-chart
fig = cs.figure(None, "EUR/MWh", height=420)
cs.add_line(fig, mf.index, mf["ptf_spread_eur"], "prices", "ptf", name="Daily spread (max − min)",
            unit=" EUR/MWh", hover_fmt=",.1f", end_label=False)
cs.add_line(fig, mf.index, mf["ptf_std_eur"], "single", "", name="Hourly standard deviation",
            unit=" EUR/MWh", hover_fmt=",.1f", end_label=False)
fig.update_layout(margin=dict(t=40))
fig.update_xaxes(rangeselector=dict(buttons=[dict(count=3, label="3Y", step="year", stepmode="backward"),
                                             dict(count=5, label="5Y", step="year", stepmode="backward"),
                                             dict(step="all", label="All")],
                                    x=1, xanchor="right", y=1.03, yanchor="bottom"))
cs.mode_buttons(fig, [
    dict(label="EUR/MWh", y=[mf["ptf_spread_eur"], mf["ptf_std_eur"]], title="EUR/MWh", hover=[",.1f"] * 2, hover_unit=" EUR/MWh"),
    dict(label="TL/MWh", y=[mf["ptf_spread"], mf["ptf_std"]], title="TL/MWh", hover=[",.0f"] * 2, hover_unit=" TL/MWh"),
    dict(label="% of average PTF", y=[mf["ptf_spread_pct"], mf["ptf_std_pct"]], title="% of the month's average PTF",
         suffix="%", hover=[",.0f"] * 2, hover_unit="%"),
])
cs.style_controls(fig)
cs.show(fig)
```

## The cost of being out of balance

When the system is short, the operator buys extra energy in the balancing market and SMF usually rises above PTF. When it is long, SMF usually falls below PTF. The gap is what a market participant risks by being out of balance in that direction: imbalance prices are built from PTF and SMF. Bars show the monthly average gap, split by system direction, in euros, lira or as a percentage of the month's average PTF. The percentage is the best way to compare years: a gap of 300 TL/MWh meant much more in 2016 than it does today.

```{python}
#| label: gap-chart
fig2 = cs.figure(None, "SMF − PTF, EUR/MWh", height=420)
g = mf.loc["2014-04-01":]
cs.add_bar(fig2, g.index, g["gap_when_short_eur"], "balancing", "up", step=1,
           name="System short: SMF above PTF", hover_fmt=",.1f", unit=" EUR/MWh")
cs.add_bar(fig2, g.index, g["gap_when_long_eur"], "balancing", "down", step=1,
           name="System long: SMF below PTF", hover_fmt=",.1f", unit=" EUR/MWh")
fig2.update_layout(barmode="relative", bargap=0.15, margin=dict(t=40))
cs.mode_buttons(fig2, [
    dict(label="EUR/MWh", y=[g["gap_when_short_eur"], g["gap_when_long_eur"]], title="SMF − PTF, EUR/MWh", hover=[",.1f"] * 2, hover_unit=" EUR/MWh"),
    dict(label="TL/MWh", y=[g["gap_when_short"], g["gap_when_long"]], title="SMF − PTF, TL/MWh", hover=[",.0f"] * 2, hover_unit=" TL/MWh"),
    dict(label="% of average PTF", y=[g["gap_when_short_pct"], g["gap_when_long_pct"]], title="SMF − PTF, % of the month's average PTF",
         suffix="%", hover=[",.0f"] * 2, hover_unit="%"),
])
fig2.update_xaxes(rangeselector=dict(buttons=[dict(count=3, label="3Y", step="year", stepmode="backward"),
                                              dict(count=5, label="5Y", step="year", stepmode="backward"),
                                              dict(step="all", label="All")],
                                     x=1, xanchor="right", y=1.03, yanchor="bottom"))
cs.style_controls(fig2)
cs.show(fig2)
```

```{python}
#| label: gap-note
pk = g["gap_when_short_pct"].idxmax()
prev = g["gap_when_short"].loc[pk - pd.DateOffset(years=1): pk - pd.DateOffset(months=1)].median()
txt = (f"The highest short-side gap in percentage terms is {pk:%B %Y}: SMF was {g.loc[pk, 'gap_when_short']:,.0f} TL/MWh "
       f"above PTF while the month's average PTF was only {g.loc[pk, 'ptf_mean']:,.0f} TL/MWh, so the gap equals "
       f"{g.loc[pk, 'gap_when_short_pct']:.0f}% of the average price. ")
if g.loc[pk, "gap_when_short"] > 1.5 * prev:
    txt += (f"The lira gap itself was also well above the {prev:,.0f} TL/MWh median of the previous twelve months: "
            f"when day-ahead prices were low, balancing prices did not fall with them. ")
txt += "Percentages exaggerate gaps in months with a low average PTF, so read them next to the lira and euro views."
Markdown(txt)
```

## Intraday versus day-ahead

The intraday market (GİP) trades the same hours after the day-ahead auction. Its average price (AOF) minus PTF shows whether buying later was cheaper or dearer on average. A gap close to zero means the two markets agree; persistent gaps point to forecasts that changed after the auction, for example for wind and solar.

```{python}
#| label: aof-chart
fig3 = cs.figure(None, "AOF − PTF, EUR/MWh", height=380)
a = mf.loc["2015-07-01":]
cs.add_bar(fig3, a.index, a["aof_ptf_gap_eur"], "markets", "gip", name="AOF − PTF", hover_fmt=",.2f", unit=" EUR/MWh")
fig3.update_layout(showlegend=False, bargap=0.15, margin=dict(t=40))
cs.mode_buttons(fig3, [
    dict(label="EUR/MWh", y=[a["aof_ptf_gap_eur"]], title="AOF − PTF, EUR/MWh", hover=[",.2f"], hover_unit=" EUR/MWh"),
    dict(label="TL/MWh", y=[a["aof_ptf_gap"]], title="AOF − PTF, TL/MWh", hover=[",.1f"], hover_unit=" TL/MWh"),
    dict(label="% of average PTF", y=[a["aof_ptf_gap_pct"]], title="AOF − PTF, % of the month's average PTF",
         suffix="%", hover=[",.2f"], hover_unit="%"),
])
cs.style_controls(fig3)
cs.show(fig3)
```

## Hours at zero

PTF falls to zero when supply that cannot or will not reduce output, such as run-of-river hydro, wind, solar and must-run plants, exceeds demand. Zero-price hours are a sign of surplus and of the value of storage and flexible demand.

```{python}
#| label: zero-chart
fig4 = cs.figure(None, "Hours per month", height=360)
cs.add_bar(fig4, mf.index, mf["ptf_zero_hours"], "single", "", name="Hours with PTF = 0", hover_fmt=",.0f", unit=" hours")
fig4.update_layout(showlegend=False, bargap=0.15, margin=dict(t=16))
cs.show(fig4)
```

## Yearly summary

```{python}
#| label: yearly
yy = d.groupby(d.index.year)
tab = pd.DataFrame({
    "Daily spread (EUR/MWh)": yy["ptf_spread_eur"].mean().map(lambda v: fmt(v, 1)),
    "Hourly std. dev. (EUR/MWh)": yy["ptf_std_eur"].mean().map(lambda v: fmt(v, 1)),
    "SMF − PTF when short": yy["gap_when_short_eur"].mean().map(lambda v: fmt(v, 1)),
    "SMF − PTF when long": yy["gap_when_long_eur"].mean().map(lambda v: fmt(v, 1)),
    "AOF − PTF": yy["aof_ptf_gap_eur"].mean().map(lambda v: fmt(v, 2)),
    "SMF − PTF when short (% of PTF)": (yy["gap_when_short"].mean() / yy["ptf_mean"].mean() * 100).map(lambda v: fmt(v, 1) + "%"),
    "SMF − PTF when long (% of PTF)": (yy["gap_when_long"].mean() / yy["ptf_mean"].mean() * 100).map(lambda v: fmt(v, 1) + "%"),
    "AOF − PTF (% of PTF)": (yy["aof_ptf_gap"].mean() / yy["ptf_mean"].mean() * 100).map(lambda v: fmt(v, 1) + "%"),
    "Zero-price hours": yy["ptf_zero_hours"].sum().map(lambda v: fmt(v)),
}).loc[2012:].sort_index(ascending=False)
tab = tab.apply(lambda c: c.str.replace("-", "−", regex=False))
tab.index = [f"{y} (to {last:%d %b})" if y == last.year else str(y) for y in tab.index]
Markdown(tab.to_markdown(disable_numparse=True, colalign=["left"] + ["right"] * len(tab.columns)))
```

Gaps in euros are converted from lira at the exchange rate implied by EPİAŞ's own lira and euro prices for each day; percentages divide the average gap by the average PTF of the same period. Yearly figures are averages of daily values; zero-price hours are totals.

### Download the data

```{python}
#| label: downloads
cols = {"ptf_spread": "ptf_daily_spread_try_mwh", "ptf_spread_eur": "ptf_daily_spread_eur_mwh",
        "ptf_std": "ptf_hourly_std_try_mwh", "ptf_std_eur": "ptf_hourly_std_eur_mwh",
        "smf_ptf_gap": "smf_minus_ptf_try_mwh", "gap_when_short": "smf_minus_ptf_when_short_try_mwh",
        "gap_when_long": "smf_minus_ptf_when_long_try_mwh", "aof_ptf_gap": "aof_minus_ptf_try_mwh",
        "ptf_zero_hours": "hours_ptf_zero", "deficit_share": "share_hours_system_short",
        "smf_ptf_gap_eur": "smf_minus_ptf_eur_mwh", "gap_when_short_eur": "smf_minus_ptf_when_short_eur_mwh",
        "gap_when_long_eur": "smf_minus_ptf_when_long_eur_mwh", "aof_ptf_gap_eur": "aof_minus_ptf_eur_mwh",
        "smf_ptf_gap_pct": "smf_minus_ptf_pct_of_ptf", "gap_when_short_pct": "smf_minus_ptf_when_short_pct_of_ptf",
        "gap_when_long_pct": "smf_minus_ptf_when_long_pct_of_ptf", "aof_ptf_gap_pct": "aof_minus_ptf_pct_of_ptf"}
dm = m[list(cols)].rename(columns=cols).round(4)
dm.index = dm.index.strftime("%Y-%m")
dd = d[list(cols)].rename(columns=cols).round(4)
dd.index = dd.index.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
stamp = f"{last:%Y%m%d}"
HTML(
    cs.download_link(dm.rename_axis("month").reset_index(), f"trpowerlab_volatility_monthly_{stamp}.csv", "Monthly (CSV)")
    + cs.download_link(dd.rename_axis("date").reset_index(), f"trpowerlab_volatility_daily_{stamp}.csv", "Daily (CSV)")
)
```

Monthly spreads and standard deviations are averages of daily values. Please credit *TR Power Lab, based on EPİAŞ Şeffaflık Platformu data*; the figures are ours under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), the underlying data belong to EPİAŞ.

## Notes

- **Source:** EPİAŞ Şeffaflık Platformu hourly PTF, SMF, system direction and intraday weighted average price, through [eptr2](https://github.com/Tideseed/eptr2). Data to `{python} f"{last:%d %B %Y}"`.
- **Price caps** limit how high prices and spreads can go; the cap has changed several times since 2022.
